item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
This table shows the ages of the girls and boys in a club.

| Age | Number of Girls | Number of Boys |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | 4 | 6 |
| 9 | 8 | 4 |
| 10 | 6 | 10 |

Use the information in the table to complete the graph for ages 9 and 10.

[Image: Double bar graph]

descriptors: All 4 bars correct for height, placement, and shading.
All 4 bars of correct height; either bars misplaced or bars shaded incorrectly in no more than one set (i.e., for age 9 or age 10).
Placement, shading, and height all correct for one, two, or three bars. (At least one bar completely correct).
All 4 bars of correct height, but two or more errors involving placement or shading.
Work is shown, but no bars are drawn. For example: only numbers are shown on the graph.

item.figure_description: An incomplete double bar graph. The vertical axis is labeled "Number" with tick marks and horizontal grid lines at 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. The horizontal axis is labeled "Age" with positions for 8, 9, and 10. A legend in the upper right shows a dark grey shaded square labeled "Girls" and an unshaded (white) square labeled "Boys". For age 8, two bars are plotted: a grey shaded bar of height 4 (Girls) followed by an adjacent white unshaded bar of height 6 (Boys). For ages 9 and 10, no bars are drawn.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.

step1.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's step 1 parameter d1? In the GPCM, b - d1 is the ability at which earning the first point becomes more likely than earning no point, so a higher d1 means that this point is earned at a lower ability; the steps sum to 0. Choose the value closest to it.
